sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and request type addition
sections.what: Brings in the Express types and the crypto library, and adds an optional correlation ID field to the request type.
sections.why: Lets the rest of the code read the ID with type safety.

sections.name: correlationId
sections.title: Assigns a tracking ID to each request
sections.what: Uses the caller's correlation ID header if present, otherwise creates a new random ID, and stores it on the request before continuing.
sections.why: Lets one request be followed through the logs, and lets callers supply their own ID to link related calls.
sections.watch_out: The caller's header value is stored exactly as sent, so it should be validated before anything relies on its format.

summary: Gives every incoming web request a tracking ID, reusing the caller's ID when one is sent.
purpose: Lets someone match server log lines to a single request. Likely purpose, since the logging code is not in this file.
why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the usual purpose of request tracking.
how: 1. Reads the x-correlation-id header from the request. 2. If it is missing or empty, creates a random UUID. 3. Stores the ID on the request. 4. Passes control to the next step.
inputs: The incoming HTTP request and its optional x-correlation-id header.
outputs: The request gains a correlationId value for later steps. Nothing is sent back to the caller.
risks: The caller's ID is trusted without length or character checks, so odd values can reach the logs. The ID is not returned in responses, so callers cannot quote it when reporting a problem.
debug: If logs show no IDs, check that this middleware is registered before the logging code. Send a request with a custom header and confirm the same value appears in the logs.
